manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Pick up the phone on the box and place it on the phone stand to the right.

Task description: The object is the black-screen phone with a light frame on the white box to the left. The target is the white phone stand to its right with an inclined back panel. Transfer the phone to the stand so it is securely supported.

Success criteria: The phone is on the stand to the right and remains securely supported by it after the gripper opens, without slipping or tipping.

## Execution tips

- There is a pen and mouse beside the phone. Choose corresponding grasp points with clearance beside both long edges, and set the opening slightly wider than the phone there to avoid grasping the pen or disturbing nearby objects.
- Choose a frame area away from the end intended to seat, but not too close to the upper corner. This balances pad contact area and leaves space for the lower end to meet the support hook.
- The phone is close to the box surface. Before closing, confirm the fingers actually surround both frame edges rather than press the screen or grip the box rim. If frame contact is insufficient, adjust the approach angle slightly rather than pushing hard along the box.
- When adjusting the phone's tilt, leave clearance between the phone and gripper and the box surface and phone stand to avoid sweeping the phone edge into them. If the current pose works, no repeated adjustment is needed.
- When seating the phone, let its lower edge enter the support range of both hooks and gently rest its back against the backplate, avoiding pushing the stand. Open the gripper gradually after confirming that the stand supports the load. If it slides or tilts, retain the grasp and adjust the contact position.

narration: I will use the piper-control skill to start this real-robot episode strictly with the specified parameters and act on the returned manual and live observations. When finished or unable to continue, I will call finish_episode.

I have read the returned manual and confirmed that the target phone is on the white box, with the phone stand to its right. I am adjusting the approach direction from above, first aligning with both side frames while avoiding the nearby pen and mouse.

An orientation adjustment hit a controller position limit, and the tool returned a recoverable rejection after partial arm movement. I replanned using the new measured pose and completed the next approach step, continuing to check reachable poses.

The gripper is open to about 84.5 mm and aligning with the phone's long-edge grasp positions. Next I will reduce approach steps, confirm the fingers surround the frame, close, and first lift slightly to check the grasp.

The fingers are nearly aligned with the phone's long edges, and the phone is still supported by the box surface. I am using small steps from millimeters to centimeters to check pad height and clearance from the nearby pen; a grasp has not yet been confirmed.

The first small lift did not make it clear whether the phone moved stably with the gripper. Above the box surface, I will reopen and adjust the grasp depth, then transfer it after confirming a secure hold.

Contact was detected on the previous closure, but the opening narrowed during lifting while the phone stayed on the box, indicating a shallow grasp. I recentered and lowered a few millimeters and am checking for fuller frame contact.

The phone has now left the box surface with the gripper. After continued lifting, the opening remains approximately 74.8 mm, and the image supports a stable grasp. I will lift further to allow rotation clearance for the phone ends, then move toward the stand on the right.

The phone rotated into a hanging pose during lifting, but the grasp stayed stable at rest and during lateral motion. I am using both views to align it with the stand and leave room for its lower edge to enter the hooks.

The phone has reached the front of the stand, and the grasp opening remains stable. I am aligning its lower edge with the two hooks in movements no larger than 1 cm and will release only after confirming the stand bears its weight.

The phone's lower edge has entered the support range of both hooks and appears nearly seated. I will maintain the grasp, make smaller adjustments to bring its back toward the panel, then gradually reduce grip force and check stability.

After further gripper release, the phone slipped off the stand onto the table, failing the stable-placement condition. Its condition requires on-site inspection after the fall. I will end this episode without another grasp; the operator should inspect the phone and stand.
